meta.title: Water, flood control and disaster policy, 19 days of posts
meta.subject: water, flood control and disaster policy in Texas — the Texas Water Fund and water supply projects, Harris County Flood Control District and flood bonds, the Hill Country floods and Camp Mystic, youth camp safety rules and the DSHS Sunset review, flood warning systems, and disaster recovery funding
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 19, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Texas water, flood control and disaster policy, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Warnings and forecasts worked
lanes.description: Posts relay live flash flood warnings, river rises and forecasts as proof that the warning system works, and urge people to turn around rather than drive into floodwater, sometimes defending forecasters against 'fear mongering' claims.

lanes.label: Honor victims with new laws
lanes.description: Officials and advocates say the July 4, 2025 Hill Country deaths demand concrete action, such as camp safety rules, warning systems and flood funding, so a repeat never happens.

lanes.label: Camp Mystic grief and healing
lanes.description: Human-interest posts about bereaved families, survivors and public figures remembering the girls lost at Camp Mystic, focused on mourning and resilience rather than blame.

lanes.label: Harris County flood money failures
lanes.description: Harris County Flood Control District is accused of failing to deliver projects despite Harvey relief and bond money, with state and federal officials pressing it on deadlines and oversight.

lanes.label: Left mocked Christian flood victims
lanes.description: Partisan claim that liberals cheered or mocked the Camp Mystic deaths because the victims were Christian or conservative, grouped with reactions to Charlie Kirk's killing.

lanes.label: Preventable deaths, no accountability
lanes.description: Argues the Camp Mystic deaths were preventable and blames camp owners and local politicians, for example for refusing aid or warnings, while noting nobody has been charged and that investigations are ongoing.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.

posts.name: Max Velocity
posts.text:
Extreme rainfall rates of up to 4 inches per hour will drive a HIGHLY DANGEROUS flash flood threat along the Texas I-35 corridor and Hill Country today!!!

As a slow-moving cold front stalls over south-central Texas, a Moderate Risk for excessive rainfall is in effect from Dallas-Fort Worth down through Austin and San Antonio. Intense thunderstorms will repeatedly train over these highly sensitive, flood-prone areas. With extreme localized rainfall rates reaching 3 to 4 inches per hour, rapid and life-threatening urban flooding is a major concern. The highest overall totals will target Deep South Texas near the Rio Grande Village, where widespread amounts exceeding 5 inches are highly probable.

Further north, historic, near-record atmospheric moisture tied to the remnants of Hurricane Polo is surging into the Midwest. This has prompted a massive Slight Risk stretching from Texas all the way to Wisconsin. Population centers across eastern Iowa and Illinois will face the heaviest of this northern rain shield this morning, picking up an additional 1 to 3 inches of rain before a cold front finally sweeps the threat away.

posts.name: Senator John Cornyn
posts.text:
On July 4, 2025, catastrophic flooding devastated Central Texas, taking the lives of 139 people, including 27 young girls at Camp Mystic, and bringing our entire state to its knees in prayer.

We cannot bring them back, but we can honor their memories by taking action to prevent another tragedy like this. I’m proud the Senate passed @RepPfluger and my Mystic Alerts Act last night.

This bill will ensure Texans, and all Americans, can receive wireless emergency alerts on their mobile devices via satellite, even when cellular networks are compromised. When disaster strikes, every second matters, and this legislation will undoubtedly save lives. I look forward to seeing this bill signed into law by @POTUS.

https://t.co/N8NA3xT9vk

posts.name: Kentucky Girl
posts.text:
It's been 15 months since 25 little girls and 2 counselors died at Camp Mystic.

A tragedy of biblical proportions.

Nobody has been charged.

On July 4, 2025, the Guadalupe River came roaring through a century-old Christian girls' camp in the Texas Hill Country. 

The families call them Heaven's 27.

Now the Texas Rangers are closing in. 

Their search warrants list possible charges against Camp Mystic: 

🔴 Manslaughter 
🔴 Criminally negligent homicide
🔴 Child endangerment
🔴 Injury to a child
🔴 Deadly conduct.

The Rangers' investigator says he believes the Eastland family's phones hold evidence of "conscious disregard of recognized hazards" and what camp leaders knew while it was happening.

So what is the family that owned the camp doing? 
Fighting it.

Their lawyers call the warrants a "fishing expedition" and want them narrowed. 

The Rangers just seized 8 iPhones and 2 Apple Watches from a family storage unit. 

Investigators still can't look at them while the privilege fight plays out.

Meanwhile, the local DA recused herself over her ties to the area and a past working relationship with an Eastland.

And in June, the camp filed for bankruptcy, which froze every wrongful-death lawsuit those families filed.

On Friday, a federal judge ruled the lawsuits can move forward Nov. 9. 

He'll decide by Oct. 19 whether the Eastlands keep control of the bankruptcy or an independent trustee takes over.

If your phones would clear you, you'd hand them over.

These parents put their daughters on a bus to summer camp. 

They deserve every text, every call, and every answer.

Justice for Heaven's 27.
